content: Noah probably did not do much fishing on the ark. He only had two worms, and he could not spare either one.
Moses was the first man with a tablet, and he got his downloads straight from the cloud.
Jonah learned you cannot keep a good man down. Even the great fish could not stomach him for more than three days.
Pharaoh refused to admit his troubles for the longest time. He was stuck in denial, which, as everyone knows, is a long river in Egypt.
The wife of Lot looked back and became a pillar of salt. I looked back at my old school pictures tonight and nearly did the same.
Zacchaeus was a short man with a tall faith. He also had the best seat at the parade.
Samson was the strongest man alive until he got a haircut. I have had a few haircuts like that myself.
Two of every animal, and not one complaint about the menu for over a year. Noah must have been a better cook than I am.
The Israelites ate manna for forty years. Somewhere in that wilderness a mother was surely saying, if you do not want manna, there is always tomorrow.
Jonah spent three days inside a great fish. I imagine he never looked at a tuna sandwich the same way again.
Daniel spent the whole night with the lions and never got a scratch. I suppose they knew better than to go lion around with a praying man.
Methuselah lived nine hundred sixty nine years. Just imagine the candles on that cake. The fire department would have needed an invitation.
Joseph had a coat of many colors. I have a coat of many coffee stains, which is nearly the same thing.
Jesus fed five thousand with five loaves and two fish. Our church tries to do the same at every potluck, and somehow there are always leftover deviled eggs.
Paul wrote half the New Testament in letters from prison. Meanwhile I cannot get a thank you card into the mail on time.
Balaam had a donkey that talked to him. My car talks to me too, but all it ever says is check engine.
Esau traded his birthright for a bowl of stew. I have been that hungry at a church potluck, but I still held on to my seat by the ham.
Peter and the others fished all night and caught nothing. Friends, I have had overnight shifts like that too.
Nicodemus came to see Jesus at night. I like to think of him as the very first overnight listener.
Paul preached so long one night that a young man named Eutychus dozed off and fell out of a window. So if I put you to sleep tonight, please stay away from the windows.
Jacob wrestled an angel all night long. Some nights I wrestle a fitted sheet, and I am fairly sure the angel was easier.
Jacob once used a stone for a pillow. Every motel I have ever stayed in has tried to keep that tradition alive.
Adam was the only man in history who never had to sit through his parents showing his baby pictures to company.
Goliath did not take young David seriously. It turned out to be a very rocky start to his day.
David played the harp beautifully, and King Saul threw a spear at him. That has to be the worst music review in history.
Elijah was fed by ravens in the wilderness. My meals come from a vending machine, which is far less miraculous but still a blessing at four in the morning.
John the Baptist lived on locusts and wild honey. I am sure it was healthy, but I will be keeping my granola bar.
Martha was busy in the kitchen while Mary sat at the feet of Jesus. Every church kitchen since has had at least one Martha, and thank the Lord for her.
The builders at Babel could not understand one another. I feel the same way every time my grandson explains his video games to me.
Thomas wanted to see the proof before he would believe. He would have made an excellent church treasurer.
Matthew collected taxes before he followed Jesus. I bet he was the one who counted the twelve baskets of leftovers.
Sarah laughed when she heard she would have a baby in her old age. I laugh too, every time I try to get up off the floor.
Jonah is the only man in the Bible who was truly swallowed up in his work.
The Israelites crossed the Red Sea on dry ground. I cannot even cross my kitchen at midnight without stepping on a squeaky dog toy.
Joshua told the sun to stand still, and it did. I tell my alarm clock the same thing every morning, and it never listens.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came. And you thought you were too old to start a new project.
Noah must have been a wonderful listener. With all those animals on board, he heard every side of the story.
Noah ran the first cruise line in history, and in all that time he never lost a single suitcase.
The frogs in Egypt must have been terribly loud at night. It makes me thankful the only thing croaking around here at four in the morning is my voice.
Abraham was promised descendants as many as the stars. Can you imagine the name tag table at that family reunion?
Isaac was named for laughter. I imagine every time somebody called him in for supper, the whole tent smiled.
Jonah tried to hide from God on a boat. He found out there is no good hiding place from the One who made the ocean.
The shepherds were working the night shift when the angels showed up. To this day, the night crew gets the best announcements.
The wise men brought gold, frankincense and myrrh. My grandmother says wise women would have brought a casserole, a warm blanket and a thank you note.
Lazarus surely had the most surprising family dinner in history. Everyone was dressed for a funeral, and he showed up hungry.
Peter tried walking on water and did fine until he looked at the wind. I do the same thing with my bank statement.
Moses climbed the mountain and came down with ten commandments. If I climbed that mountain at my age, I would come down with ten complaints.
Elijah went to heaven in a whirlwind. At my age, I need a whirlwind just to get out of the recliner.
Noah did not need a weather app. He had a much more reliable forecast.
The Bible says the Lord gives His beloved sleep. Some nights I think He is waiting for me to stop talking first.
Solomon asked God for wisdom instead of riches. I asked for wisdom too, and somehow I still bought the extended warranty.
The walls of Jericho came down after seven days of marching. My grandson can bring down a block tower in seven seconds, and he does not even need a trumpet.
Gideon put out a fleece to hear from God. These days I put out a fleece and the cat sleeps on it.
Job had patience like no one else. Then again, he never waited on hold with the phone company.
Noah had a dove, a raven, and two of everything else. My house has two cats, a dog, and a goldfish, and I am already outnumbered.
The prodigal son came home and got the fattened calf. If I come home late, I get a plate in the microwave and a note on the counter, and I am grateful for both.
Hezekiah was given fifteen more years of life. I would settle for fifteen more minutes of sleep.
The manger had no room service, no wake up call, and no pillow mints. And yet it was the finest room in all of history.
Adam and Eve had the perfect garden, and they still found the one thing they were not supposed to touch. My grandchildren would have done the same thing by lunchtime.
Jonah was the first man to go whale watching from the inside.
Moses parted the Red Sea. I cannot even part my hair anymore, because there is not enough left to part.
Pharaoh had ten plagues and still did not listen. I have one dripping faucet, and it gets my attention every single night.
An old church bulletin once announced a potluck supper at five, with prayer and medication to follow.
Years ago a church bulletin read, do not let worry kill you, let the church help. I think they meant that kindly.
One bulletin I saw said the morning sermon would be Jesus walks on the water, and the evening sermon would be searching for Jesus.
Our bulletin once announced that the eighth graders would present Hamlet in the fellowship hall, and everyone was invited to attend this tragedy.
Last week the bulletin said the choir would be singing, I Will Not Pass This Way Again. The ushers said that was good to know for planning purposes.
Hymnals are the only books where everybody reads the first verse, the second verse, and the last verse, and quietly skips the third like it owes them money.
Nobody really knows what the third verse of most hymns says. It may be the best kept secret in the whole church.
Church coffee is a true mystery. It is somehow lukewarm and far too strong at the very same time.
The coffee in our fellowship hall is so strong, it stood up on its own for the doxology.
Our pastor promised a short sermon this morning. He meant short compared to eternity.
Somebody asked our pastor how long he preaches. He said, until I am done, or until the smell of fried chicken from the fellowship hall wins.
Our church organist can play any hymn in any key, as long as it is the key she likes best.
Ushers have a remarkable gift. They can find you a seat, hand you a bulletin, and count the whole room, all without missing a single amen.
An usher once asked an elderly fellow if he would like to move up front. He said, no thank you, I sat up front in nineteen fifty two and I am still recovering.
Every church has an unwritten seating chart. Sit in the wrong pew once, and you will feel twenty eyes politely asking if you are lost.
The back pew fills up first at every church I have ever attended. Folks are just leaving room up front for the Holy Spirit.
A Sunday school teacher asked her class why we should be quiet in church. One little girl raised her hand and said, because people are sleeping.

During art time at church, a little girl was busy drawing. The teacher asked what it was, and she said it was a picture of God. The teacher said nobody knows what God looks like. She said, they will in a minute.

One boy retold the story of Lot to his class. He said the wife of Lot looked back and turned into a pillar of salt, and then added that his mother looked back once while driving and turned into a telephone pole.
For years my grandson prayed, Our Father, who art in heaven, Harold be thy name. For years he thought God and his uncle Harold had a lot in common.
For a whole year my niece sang a hymn about Gladly, the cross eyed bear. To this day I cannot sing that line without smiling.
Asked why Mary and Joseph took Jesus to the temple, one boy said it was obvious. They could not find a babysitter.
One boy in Sunday school insisted the wife of Noah was named Joan of Ark.
An eager student explained that the epistles were the wives of the apostles.
The fifth commandment, according to one young scholar, is humor thy father and mother. Honestly, that is not bad advice either.
One child closed her prayer with, and please take care of yourself, God. If anything happens to You, we are in big trouble.
My granddaughter once prayed, Dear God, could You please put a few more vitamins in candy. I said amen to that one.

A grandmother asked her granddaughter what she learned in church. She said the pastor told them we come from dust and return to dust. Then she whispered, Grandma, there is somebody under my bed, and I cannot tell if they are coming or going.
Little Billy prayed at supper, Lord, thank You for the food, and thank You that Grandma cooked tonight instead of Dad.

One small boy was asked to say grace at a big family dinner. He said, I do not know what to say. His mother said, just say what you hear me say. So he bowed his head and said, Lord, why did I invite all these people.
During the children sermon, the pastor asked what is gray, has a bushy tail, and gathers nuts. A boy said, I know the answer is supposed to be Jesus, but it sure sounds like a squirrel.
A sign in our church nursery says that says, we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed. Somebody there has a gift for scripture.
When asked about the Good Samaritan, one boy said the lesson was clear. When you are in trouble, somebody should help you.
In children church, a boy said the most important thing about the Good Shepherd is that He never loses count.
After a long service, my grandson whispered loudly, if we give him the money now, will he let us go.
Last Sunday my grandson asked why the pastor wears a microphone. I said so everyone can hear him. He asked, then why does Grandpa still fall asleep.
One Easter a boy told me Jesus rose from the dead, and then he said the best part is Jesus did it without even an alarm clock.
At vacation Bible school a boy asked if Noah let the woodpeckers on the ark, and if so, how the boat stayed afloat.
According to my granddaughter, Jesus was born in Bethlehem because His parents liked to travel, and the inn was all out of cribs.
At the church picnic, a small boy asked if heaven would have a swimming pool. His grandmother said heaven will have whatever you need to be happy. He said, then I am bringing my dog.
Church potlucks have their own theology. Nobody is quite sure who made the green Jell-O salad, but everybody agrees it is a mystery best left unsolved.
At every church potluck, there is one lady with a casserole that nobody can name and everybody goes back for seconds.
At our church potluck, the line for fried chicken moves faster than any revival I have ever seen.
Potluck rule number one at our church is simple. If the dish has a spoon already in it, somebody from the choir got there first.
Church folks will argue about many things, but nobody ever argues with the lady who brings the banana pudding.
There is a covered dish my wife has she has carried to every church supper for thirty years. Nobody remembers what was in it, but everyone remembers the dish.
There is always one deviled egg left on the platter at the end of a potluck. Everybody is too polite to take the last one, so it just sits there in fellowship.
At our church supper, a fellow asked what was in the mystery casserole. The cook smiled and said, love, and whatever was left in the refrigerator.
The choir robes at our church have been around so long, they have seen three pastors, two building programs, and one very memorable Christmas cantata.
In every church choir there is one fellow who sings bass so low that the pews hum along with him.
Our choir director says we should all watch her hands. Some of us have been watching for years, and we still come in a measure early.
Church business meetings are the only meetings where the motion to adjourn gets a louder amen than the sermon.
A church sign near me said, come in for a faith lift. I thought that was a good offer.
Another church sign read, sign broken, message inside. I have been meaning to stop by.
One church sign said, if you are headed in the wrong direction, God allows U turns.
A church sign I passed said, free trip to heaven, details inside. I liked that one so much I turned around and read it twice.
Some church signs make you think. One near me simply said, exposure to the Son may prevent burning. Another said, prayer, the best wireless connection.
A sign outside a country church read, we are not dead yet, come see for yourself on Sunday. I appreciated the honesty.
Church greeters are the only people who can shake your hand, ask about your mother, and remember your dog by name, all in about four seconds.
The church nursery workers deserve a special crown in heaven. Possibly two, if it was a Sunday with a full moon.
No church is complete without a thermostat committee. Half want it warmer, half want it cooler, and the Lord is the only one who stays perfectly comfortable.
The church bus at my old church had so many miles on it, it remembered when gas was a quarter.
Vacation Bible school is a wonderful week. The children go home full of joy, and the volunteers go home full of glitter.
Every church has at least one person who sits in the same seat for forty years. If you sit there by mistake, you are in for a gracious but very long stare.
A choir member once asked me if I sing. I said only when no one is around. She said, that seems wise.
My pastor says he preaches to the choir every week, and he still cannot get them to come in on time.
The best part about a church fellowship dinner is that nobody counts calories. We are told the blessing takes care of them.
Our church has been raising money for a new steeple for years. At this rate, the Lord may come back before the steeple goes up.
Some folks pray for rain, and some pray for sunshine. At our church picnic, we just pray for enough ice in the cooler.
Down in the church kitchen we have seven coffee makers. Nobody knows which one works, so we just make coffee in all of them and pray.
When a sermon goes long, I like to remember that Paul once preached until midnight. Our pastor is just honoring tradition.
The deacon at my old church could pray so long over the meal that the iced tea turned into hot tea.
I have reached the age where I walk into a room, forget why I came, and decide to pray about it while I am there.
My memory is not what it used to be. Then again, I cannot remember what it used to be.
I told my grandson I was going to bed early tonight. He asked if I meant early for me, or early for regular people.
You know you are getting older when you bend down to tie your shoe and look around for anything else you can do while you are down there.
Nobody needs to rain on my parade anymore. My knees will forecast it a full day ahead.
They say age is just a number. Mine has gotten so big it needs its own zip code.
You know you are getting up there when the birthday candles cost more than the cake.
My grandson asked me how old I am. I told him I was around when the Dead Sea was only feeling a little under the weather.
My grandchildren think I am a computer genius because I know how to turn it off and turn it back on again.
At my age, I do not get lost anymore. I just take the scenic route on purpose, every single time.
The older I get, the earlier it gets late.
My doctor told me to start walking more. So now I walk to the refrigerator twice as often.
The doctor asked if I get winded climbing stairs. I said, only the ones that go up.
Getting older means your get up and go has got up and went. Thankfully, my sit down and stay is in perfect working order.
I finally have everything figured out at my age. Unfortunately, I cannot remember where I wrote it all down.
At my age, a big night out means I stayed up past the weather report.
These days I am a lot like an old hymn. A little slow, a few verses too long, but still worth singing.
My knees make more noise than the church organ. At least the organ can stay in tune.
I used to have a photographic memory. These days it never seems to have any film in it.
Some days I feel like a spring chicken. Most days I feel like the chicken that spring forgot.
My grandmother always said, an old fiddle still plays a sweet tune. Then she would add, it just takes longer to tune it.
I keep my reading glasses on a chain around my neck now. That way I only lose the chain.
I asked my wife where my glasses were. She said, on your face. I said, well, that would explain why I can see you so clearly.
At my age, I have learned that a nap is not a sign of weakness. It is a sign of wisdom with a pillow.
Grandparents are simply parents who finally have time to enjoy the children, plus the privilege of handing them back.

My granddaughter asked why my hair turned gray. I said each gray hair is from something her mother did as a child. She thought for a while and said, then you must have been a handful for Great Grandma.
My grandson asked if I had a computer when I was young. I said yes, it was called a pencil, and it never once needed an update.
When my grandkids come over, I am the fun grandpa. When they leave, I am the tired grandpa who sleeps on the couch with the remote on his chest.
My grandmother used to say, if you cannot say something nice, come sit next to me on the porch and we will pray about them together.
Grandmas have a special gift. They can tell you that you look too thin while they hand you your third slice of pie.
Somebody young once told me I was older than dirt. I told him that is not true, because the Lord made dirt first and then made me out of it.
A grandchild is the only person who can wake you at five in the morning and make you thankful for it.
A grandchild asked me what life was like before television. I said it was quieter, the stars were brighter, and Grandma talked a lot more.
Grandpa says he does not snore. He just dreams out loud about logging.
Grandkids think everything Grandpa says is a story, and everything Grandma says is the truth. They are usually right on both counts.
Little Sam asked if I knew any famous people. I said I knew a man who could play every hymn in the book on a harmonica, and he was very impressed.
My coffee and I have a quiet agreement. I do not ask how strong it is, and it does not ask how tired I am.
I do not have a coffee problem. I have a coffee solution, and it works about every two hours.
Somebody asked me how I take my coffee. I said, very seriously, especially after midnight.
Decaf at four in the morning is like singing a hymn with the words left out. It just does not do the job.
My coffee mug says world best grandpa. My grandson bought it for me, and I have decided to believe it.
I tried to give up coffee once. It was the longest forty minutes of my life.
I measure my overnight shift in cups of coffee. Tonight we are somewhere around cup three and a half.
The coffee pot in our studio has been brewing since the Carter years. It still makes a decent cup, and so do I.
If you cannot sleep right now, do not worry. Counting sheep is fine, but talking to the Shepherd works even better, and He is awake anyway.
Insomnia is when your body goes to bed, and your brain decides it is the perfect time to reorganize the garage.
I asked the Lord for a good night of sleep years ago, and He gave me an overnight radio show. He has a wonderful sense of humor.
My pillow has a cool side for exactly four minutes. After that, we are just two old friends getting through the night together.
Here is a mystery for the ages. I am wide awake at three in the morning, and sound asleep at three in the afternoon.
Doctors say you should not look at screens before bed. So I lie there and look at the ceiling instead, and the ceiling has very few new ideas.
The best way to fall asleep is to try very hard to stay awake. Just ask anyone who ever sat through a slide show of vacation pictures.
I tried counting sheep last night. Around number four hundred, one of them asked if he could go home.
My wife can fall asleep in seven seconds. I need seven minutes, two prayers, and one last trip to check the front door.
Some folks have a sleep number on their bed. My number is however many pages of Leviticus I can read before my eyes close.
I read that people sleep better in a cool, dark, quiet room. That explains why I sleep so well in church.
They say you should go to bed at the same time every night. I do, it just happens to be eight in the morning.
I bought one of those machines that plays ocean sounds to help me sleep. Now I dream about Jonah all night.
If you are lying awake right now, staring at the ceiling, wave at it for me. It has been keeping you company all night.
Night-shift nurses know a secret. Every patient is perfectly calm until shift change, and then everybody needs something at once.
Night-shift workers eat breakfast at supper time and supper at breakfast time. It is confusing, but nobody ever turns down a donut at any hour.
Night-shift life means your neighbors think you are on permanent vacation, because they only ever see you in your pajamas.
Truckers out there tonight, you have seen more sunrises than most poets. You just saw them through a bug splattered windshield.
To the folks working overnight, remember, the early bird gets the worm, but the night owl gets the whole quiet road.
Working nights means when somebody says good morning, you have to stop and think whether they are coming or going.
Overnight security guards have one of the toughest jobs around. They spend all night protecting a building that mostly just wants to sleep.
A night-shift nurse once told me her favorite hymn was Sweet Hour of Prayer. She said that is about all the break time she ever gets.
People sometimes ask if I talk to myself on the overnight. Not at all, I am talking to you. You are just a very good listener.
In radio, silence is called dead air. In my house, silence is called the grandchildren finally fell asleep.
I have been on the radio so long, I sometimes introduce myself at the grocery store and wait for the next song to start.
My microphone hears everything I say all night long and has never once interrupted me. That is the best friend a talker could ask for.
Folks ask how I stay awake until six in the morning. I tell them the music does half the work, and the coffee does the other three halves.
The engineer at our station says I have a voice made for radio. I am still deciding whether that is a compliment.
Being on the overnight means my lunch break is at two in the morning. Nobody else at the diner is ordering meatloaf, but I like it.
My studio chair squeaks every time I lean back. I have decided it is just singing harmony.
The best thing about overnight radio is that nobody can see that I am wearing house slippers.
I keep a little sign in the studio that says, be still and know. Some nights it is the only part of the instructions I follow.
Radio folks say you should smile when you talk, because people can hear it. So if I sound a little sleepy, just know I am smiling sleepily.
My cat attends every evening prayer at my house. She sits right in the middle of the floor and waits for somebody to say amen and open the treat bag.
My dog has the gift of hospitality. Every stranger who walks through the door is greeted like a long lost cousin.
I knocked over my glass of water tonight, and my cat looked at me like I had committed a grave sin. Cats are very strict about who is allowed to knock things over.
My dog thinks I am the most important man in the world. My cat thinks I am the help. Between the two of them, I stay humble.
The Bible says a merry heart does good like a medicine. My dog wags his tail at me every morning, so I guess I have a prescription.
My cat sleeps about sixteen hours a day. I have never seen a creature that takes the Sabbath that seriously.
Our puppy ate a whole page of my Bible once. It was Psalm twenty three, so I figure he just wanted to lie down in green pastures.
Our dog barks at the mailman every single day. You would think by now he would have figured out that the man keeps coming back anyway.
My cat finds the one sunny spot in the house every afternoon. It is the most faithful thing she does all day.
Every night the dog waits by the door every night until I come home. I think he is the only one in the house who knows my schedule.
I told my dog he was a good boy, and he believed me completely. I wish I had that kind of faith.
Cats are wonderful company on long nights. They do not say much, and they always agree with you, as long as you keep the food coming.
My old hound dog sleeps through thunderstorms, fireworks, and the doorbell, but wakes up when I open a bag of cheese. I call that selective hearing.
Our goldfish has been with us for six years. He has heard every family argument and never taken a side, so I consider him a peacemaker.
My parakeet learned to whistle the first line of Amazing Grace. Now he will not stop, and honestly, I cannot complain.
My family has a rule at the dinner table. Whoever prays the longest gets the cold mashed potatoes.
Our family reunion has a tradition. Everybody brings a dish, everybody tells the same stories, and everybody laughs like they never heard them before.
My wife says I never listen to her. At least I think that is what she said.
My daughter asked how I knew her mother was the one. I said, because she laughed at my jokes on the very first date, and she has been patient ever since.
In every family, one relative takes all the pictures. That is why there are no pictures of that relative anywhere.
My son called and asked if I could help him move. I told him I would be glad to pray for his back.
Kids say the funniest things. My grandson told me he wanted to be a pastor when he grew up, so that he could talk all morning and nobody could interrupt him.
My mother used to say, I will give you something to cry about. She never did, but she always gave us pie.
When I was a boy, my father would say, money does not grow on trees. Then why, I asked him, do banks have so many branches.
My wife and I have been married so long that we finish each other sentences. Mostly with, where did you put the keys.
We have a junk drawer in our kitchen that I believe dates back to the book of Genesis.
Family road trips taught me to pray without ceasing. Mostly, are we there yet, Lord.
My uncle told the same joke at every Thanksgiving for forty years. By the end, we laughed because we loved him, and that is a fine reason to laugh.
My son asked me what the secret is to a long marriage. I told him, two words, yes dear. Then your mother tells me what I agreed to.
Here is a riddle for you. Who was the smartest man in the Bible? Abraham, because he knew a lot.
Riddle time. What man in the Bible had no parents? Joshua, the son of Nun.
Which Bible character is known for being the shortest? Some say Bildad the Shuhite, a shoe height. Others say Knee high Miah.
Which animal on the ark was the most honest? The cheetah could not be trusted, so it must have been the lamb.
Noah once gave the leopard a bath. The leopard said when Noah gave it a bath? That really hit the spot.
How did the animals on the ark pass the time? They played games, but they kept a close eye on the cheetahs.
Mosquitoes were scarce on the ark, because Noah only let two on, and I have been wishing ever since that he swatted them.
Which Old Testament prophet was the best at fixing things? Elisha, because he could make an iron axe head float. That is a man you want on the church building committee.
Who was the first person in the Bible to work the night shift? Some say the angels watching the shepherds, but I think it was the shepherds themselves. The angels just made the announcement.
Why was Jonah a great fisherman? He knew the inside of the business better than anyone.
When Noah saw the first rainbow, I imagine he said, finally, somebody turned off the faucet.
How do we know Peter was a fisherman? Every time he got in trouble, he said something fishy.
Which disciple loved the bakery the most? It must have been the one who kept asking for daily bread.
Noah put the kangaroos near the door, so they could hop off first and save everyone a trip.
What would Noah have done if the woodpeckers started pecking? Prayed very hard and kept a hammer handy.
Why was the ark the quietest boat on the sea? Because two of every animal were too seasick to argue.
Here is a Bible riddle my grandfather loved. What is the strongest day of the week? Sunday, because all the others are weekdays.
And another one from Grandpa. Which day is the rest of the week jealous of? Sunday, because it gets all the hymns.
The first division problem in the Bible came when God divided the light from the darkness. We are still enjoying the remainder tonight.
A shepherd brings a lantern to the field at night because he wants to keep an eye on the flock, and the flock wants to keep an eye on him.
What hymn do the overnight truckers sing? I am told it is Onward Christian Soldiers, but with more coffee.
Which hymn is a favorite among insomniacs? Abide With Me, because they figure somebody had better.
A sleepy choir favorite is Sweet By and By, which, at this hour, is exactly when I hope to wake up.
What hymn does a sleepy grandpa sing? Blessed Assurance, because he is assured he will be napping by the second verse.
What is the favorite hymn of every lost set of car keys? I Once Was Lost, but Now Am Found, usually in the other coat pocket.
What hymn should be played at every family road trip? I Need Thee Every Hour, especially if there is no rest stop for forty miles.
The favorite hymn of anyone waiting for their pie to come out of the oven? Standing on the Promises.
Which hymn is the favorite of every church janitor? Holy, Holy, Holy, as in, who left all these bulletins in the pew.
Every weather forecaster in the church choir loves There Shall Be Showers of Blessing, and the ones in Florida really mean it.
Which Bible book do insomniacs read most? Numbers, because they keep counting the hours.
At the Christmas Eve service, one candle leaned over and asked the other, are you going out tonight?
Our pews squeak because they have been listening to sermons so long, they finally have something to say.
A sheep that knows every hymn by heart is what I call a hymn lamb.
The hymnal once told the Bible, you have all the good stories, but I have all the good harmony.
That shepherd stayed up all night because he did not want to lose any of his ewes.
Any sheep who dozes off during the sermon is known as a lamb in Gilead.
A shepherd up all night with the flock was the original night watchman.
Night owls make good church members. They never miss the late service.
Every choir has one member who always arrives late. We call him a hymn in progress.
How do you know a church is friendly? When the welcome mat says amen before you even step on it.
An organist who works overnight is pulling the midnight Bach shift.
Want to stay awake during a long sermon? Sit next to a toddler with a cracker.
Why are church bells so dependable? Because they always tell the truth, and they always ring on time.
Cross a church bell with a rooster, and you get the earliest Sunday service in town.
How can you tell a deacon has been at the potluck? There is a little extra gravy on his tie, and a lot of joy on his face.
How does a sleepy pastor end his sermon? With a long, slow amen, and then he checks to see if anyone is still awake.
Our young pastor brought a pillow to the board meeting. He said he heard it might go on until morning.
Coffee has a message for every night-shift nurse. I have got your back until seven.
Truckers ought to keep a hymnal on the road. That way they will have something to read at every rest stop, and something to sing on every hill.
Night-shift nurses love the book of Psalms, because it was written by somebody who also did a lot of thinking at midnight.
Radio hosts make good shepherds. We spend all night talking to folks we cannot see and hoping nobody wanders off.
How does a radio host count sheep? With a playlist, one hymn at a time, until everybody is asleep.
The quietest thing at a radio station at four in the morning is the phone. I keep checking on it, and it is still asleep.
The alarm clock started going to church. It said it wanted to learn how to rest.
The moon told the overnight DJ, you keep the music going, I will keep the light on.
The night owl joined our church after he heard there was a late night prayer meeting and he did not want to miss it.
Why are rocking chairs so good at prayer? They spend their whole lives going back and forth to the same place.
The recliner told Grandpa, lean on me, but please, not so heavily.
Grandparents love naps. They have finally earned the right to fall asleep during their own stories.
Every pillow says the same thing to a tired head. I was hoping you would come by.
How do you know the coffee pot is a Christian? It is always full of grounds for hope.
Any dog that comes to church every week is a good, good boy with perfect attendance.
Dogs would make excellent church members. They are always happy to see you, and they never complain about the sermon length.
The cat refused to come to Bible study. She heard it was about Daniel and the lions, and she did not want her cousins to look bad.
During hymn sing, our hound sits by the piano. He likes to howl the harmony.
Every church picnic has a squirrel, and he is a nut who is truly thankful.
In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. Then He rested. I have been trying to follow the second part of that example for years.
Pastor Jim says he knows the sermon is going well when the folks in the back are nodding. He has not yet asked whether they are agreeing or sleeping.
Moses spent forty days on the mountain without a snack. At my age, I cannot make it forty minutes without checking the cookie jar.
Somebody told me patience is a virtue. I said I would think about it later.
Grandpa always said the secret to a long life is to keep breathing. He was right about that, and he also ate a lot of oatmeal.
Before cell phones, if you wanted to know where your kids were, you just stood on the porch and called them for supper. The whole county knew when it was meatloaf night.
Twelve disciples followed Jesus, and not one of them ever asked where they were parking. That is real faith.
Back in my day, we did not have streaming music. We had a church organ, a piano, and a lady named Mildred who knew every hymn by heart.
Nothing makes you feel older than when the music you grew up with is called a golden oldie. Tonight we just call it good music.
Sleep is a gift from God. Some nights I just wish He would not wrap it so tightly.
People ask why I like playing the old hymns. I tell them they are like an old pair of slippers. They fit, they are warm, and nobody else wants to borrow them.
Babies sleep like, well, babies. Which means they wake up every two hours and want a snack. Sounds a lot like Grandpa, now that I think about it.
Every new parent knows the most beautiful sound in the world. It is the silence after the baby finally falls asleep.
New parents, if you are walking the floor with a little one tonight, take heart. Someday that child will be a teenager, and you will have to wake them up for church.
Somebody once asked me if I believe in miracles. I said, I have seen a toddler sit still through a whole sermon, so yes, I believe.
Jonah went to sea, Noah went by ark, and Elijah went by chariot. I go by minivan, and honestly, I think they all had more legroom.
Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. I climbed a stepladder last week to change a light bulb, and my wife prayed the whole time.
The Psalmist said, I will lie down and sleep in peace. He clearly never had a cat that walks across his face at three in the morning.
King David danced before the Lord with all his might. I dance before the Lord too, mostly when I step on a toy in the dark.
Grandma used to say that cleanliness is next to godliness. Grandpa used to say that a nap is next to cleanliness, and he would know.
Sunday dinner at Grandma meant three kinds of meat, four kinds of vegetables, and a pie for every grandchild. Nobody ever went home hungry, and nobody ever went home without leftovers.
A quiet house at night is a blessing. Unless you have a refrigerator that hums like a gospel quartet warming up.
I tried to set up one of those smart speakers at home. Now it plays hymns when I ask for the weather, and honestly, I think it knows what I need.
It is getting late, and I know some of you are fighting sleep. I say let sleep win tonight. It has been trying so hard.
Old church pianos are like old saints. A few keys may stick, and they may be a little out of tune, but oh, the songs they still know.
I asked the Lord to give me patience, and He sent me a three year old grandson for the whole weekend. Lesson received.
Prayer requests at our church once included a lost cat, a sick cow, and a man who just wanted somebody to pray he would find his reading glasses. They were on his head.
The overnight hours are when you learn who your real friends are. Mine are the coffee pot, the hymnal, and every one of you listening.
I am convinced that the snooze button was invented by someone who loved the night shift and never wanted morning to come.
Sometimes my grandson and I just sit on the porch and say nothing at all. He thinks it is boring. I call it the deepest conversation of the week.
Moses told Pharaoh, let my people go. My grandson tells me, let my bedtime go, and he is just as determined.
